messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: HIGH severity — TLS handshake failures detected for /v1/generate in us-east-1. Error rate 6.2x baseline. Affected customers: hosted API customers, some dedicated pools. alice is on-call.

alice: acked. joining. pulling LB/envo y logs now. visible spike at ~2026-03-15T10:12:00Z on latency & tls_handshake_error count.

bob: I'm on. tailing envoy on frontends. initial look: Envoy returning 525 (TLS handshake failed) back to ALB. grabbing detailed logs.

carla: adding network team. seeing a lot of `SSL_accept` errors in backend logs and also ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages from instances to load-balancer IPs. possible MTU problem?

alice: example from envoy log:
```
[2026-03-15T10:13:01Z] TLS handshake error: SSL_accept: error:1408A0C1:SSL routines:ssl3_get_client_hello:no shared cipher
[2026-03-15T10:13:01Z] remote_addr=10.34.1.120:443 upstream: 10.12.8.47:1800
```

bob: curl from inside cluster to backend service shows TLS fail: 
```
curl -v https://10.12.8.47:1800/health
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, handshake failure (560)
* SSL: certificate subject name 'redwood-inference-internal' does not match 'api.redwood.com'
```

derived note: some clients show hostname mismatch, others show handshake record truncation. two parallel hypotheses: cert rotation / SNI mismatch OR network MTU/fragmentation causing ClientHello truncation.

carla: timeline I'm assembling: 
- 10:08 — certificate rotation job kicked by infra automation (canary to frontends)
- 10:11 — route table change pushed to peering connection between vpc-eu and vpc-us (chore:cleanup-routes job)
- 10:12 — spike in tls_handshake_error begins
- 10:13 — first customer report of SSL handshake failures to support
- 10:14 — ICMP frag-needed messages start from several ENIs

alice: assigning hypotheses:
1) cert-rotation bug: new cert missing SAN/SNI mapping -> some clients send SNI, envoy rejects -> bob to validate cert chain and SNI mapping
2) MTU/fragmentation: DF set + smaller MTU on peering path truncates ClientHello leading to handshake failure -> carla/david to check MTU, iptables, tun devices
3) VPC peering route flaps causing partial connectivity and non-TLS-aware retries -> netops to verify peering state

bob: dug into certs: `openssl x509 -in /etc/envoy/certs/current.pem -noout -subject -issuer -dates -ext subjectAltName` output:
```
subject=CN = redwood-inference-internal
X509v3 Subject Alternative Name:
    DNS:internal-service.local
Not After : Apr 01 12:00:00 2026 GMT
```
This cert indeed lacks `DNS:api.redwood.com`. rotation job seems to have pushed an internal-only cert to frontends by mistake. that explains the name mismatch. but does not fully explain fragmentation/ICMP messages.

carla: net evidence for MTU: tcpdump on eni-10.34.1.120 shows: `ICMP Destination unreachable (fragmentation needed) mtu=1436` for packets destined to 10.12.8.47 around 10:13:00Z. Also see several TCP segments where TLS ClientHello is split across fragments.

david: quick mitigation options: 
- rollback cert rotation to previous cert (fast, targeted) -> mitigates SNI/name-mismatch.
- push MTU bump (set MTU 1500 -> 9000?) across path or remove DF bit -> risky broad network change.
- re-run peering sync to ensure path stable 

erin: customers affected reporting 5xx / TLS errors. CS triage: mark broad impact and notify enterprise customers with workaround (use region fallback). prepping template.

alice: immediate plan: 
- bob to rollback cert rotation to last-known-good cert on frontends (estimated 6m) — actioned now.
- carla & david to run `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc=1` on a small canary of ENIs to test if PMTU is culprit (non-destructive, reversible).
- netops to verify peering state and route tables; look for recent automated runbooks around 10:11.

bob: rolling back certs now — switching symlink to cert-20260301 and reloading envoy on 3 frontends in staggered 30s intervals. posting outputs: 
```
# ln -sf /etc/envoy/certs/cert-20260301.pem /etc/envoy/certs/current.pem && systemctl reload envoy
reload envoy: OK (pid 12345 -> pid 12348)
```

carla: canary MTU change applied to eni-10.34.1.120 -> `ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1436` then to 1500; testing shows reduction of ICMP frag-needed. 

bob: after cert rollback, curl -v to backend from frontend: 
```
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), Server hello (2)
* SSL connection established
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
Handshake success on first checked frontends.

alice: monitoring. error rate dropping to near baseline at 10:22. marking incident as mitigated but keep the channel open for RCA.

carla: tracking remaining work: 
- audit cert rotation job — root cause: rotation pipeline templating error pointed to internal cert bundle; fix pipeline and add SNI validation step (owner: bob)
- create automated PMTU probe across peered VPCs and add alert if ICMP frag-needed > threshold (owner: carla)
- review peering route change automation; add safety guard window to prevent simultaneous route+cert changes (owner: netops)

alice: rough customer impact summary for postmortem: ~18 customers experienced degraded requests between 10:12-10:22 in us-east-1; key enterprise customers flagged for direct outreach. CS alerted.

david: logging evidence and artifacts uploaded to incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/1864567891/logs/ (envoy-logs, tcpdumps, certs, commands).

carla: hypothesis tracker (in-thread):
- H1 (cert rotation mis-deploy) — confirmed (partial) — evidence: cert metadata mismatch, rollback fixed handshake for many clients — status: confirmed, owner: bob
- H2 (PMTU fragmentation causing ClientHello truncation) — supported — evidence: ICMP frag-needed, tcpdump ClientHello split — status: likely, owner: carla
- H3 (peering route change amplifying impact) — plausible contributor — evidence: route change coincident at 10:11, need further route logs — status: under-investigation, owner: netops

alice: next steps / action items to include in RCA doc: cert pipeline fix, SNI validation test, PMTU probes, peering automation safety. I'll open the post-incident doc and assign owners.

carla: created RCA stub: https://docs.internal.redwood.com/incident/1864567891 (will fill detailed timeline + artifacts).

alice: handing on-call to bob for 1h to cover follow-ups. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. incident channel will remain open for RCA updates until 2026-03-17.

bob: sending final note: cert rollback resolved immediate customer-facing symptom. follow-ups will close root causes: pipeline templating bug + network frag tests. I'll start the cert-pipeline PR now.

carla: saving last tcpdump snippet for RCA: 
```
10:12:59.123456 IP 10.34.1.120.54321 > 10.12.8.47.1800: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1, win 64240, length 511
10:12:59.123460 IP 10.34.1.120 > 10.12.8.47: ICMP frag-needed mtu 1436
10:12:59.123500 IP 10.34.1.120.54321 > 10.12.8.47.1800: Flags [P.], seq 512:1024, length 512 (fragmented)
```

alice: closing the live mitigation phase. RCA doc and follow-ups will be tracked in the postmortem channel. thanks all for quick response.
